homeTenant.name: Ain Foundry
homeTenant.note: ownerReleases: persona releases the platform owner approved outside the studio, applied once by the deploy's seed (packages/db/src/seed/owner-releases.ts). thomas-2026-11-05 (approved 2026-11-05, ADR-0021): Corin's vEIR becomes Thomas, an AI mentor under his own name with a conversation-first doctrine. amara-seam-again-2026-11-08 (owner, 2026-11-08; packages/db/src/seed/story-releases.ts): the demo founder Amara gets a new, simple venture, Seam Again (a weekly campus clothes-repair pop-up), coached by Thomas, and leaves SoleSignal; nothing is deleted.

models.note: Owner decision 2026-11-06 (ADR-0022): the coach is Claude Haiku 4.5 through its US inference profile, with Amazon Nova 2 Lite behind it. primary and fallback serve every purpose a founder reads: a turn (its streamed reply and its fields), a recap, the distillation (it writes the notebook and the next opener) and a studio test conversation. background serves the rest on Nova 2 Lite: the safety screen (classification), evaluations, ingestion and seeding. Haiku costs about 3.3 times Nova per input token and 2.2 times per output token (packages/ai/src/pricing.ts); prompt caching (cache reads at a tenth of the input rate) takes about half of that back on a conversation's turns (docs/runbooks/latency.md). The spend caps are unchanged. A later switch to another provider's model changes these ids and the gateway adapter (packages/ai), nothing else.

luna.note: Listed for this account but invocation returns 401 'not available for this account' (account-level gating by AWS, verified 2026-10-05). Set enabled=true after AWS grants access; Luna then becomes primary with the configured primary as its fallback.

aurora.note: Pauses after 30 idle minutes (USD 0 while paused; about USD 0.06 an hour while in use at 0.5 ACU). The owner chose this over keeping it awake (about USD 44 a month). The first request after a pause waits about 15-20 s while the cluster resumes; the web app starts the resume as soon as someone opens a page (POST /api/v1/wake), so most of that wait overlaps reading or signing in (docs/runbooks/cost-controls.md, "Aurora: paused when idle").

api.note: 1,769 MB is one full vCPU on Lambda (CPU scales with memory): cold starts, session checks and every request's own work run about 1.7x faster than at 1,024 MB, for about USD 0.0000097 more per second of a running request (docs/runbooks/latency.md).

speech.note: Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe streaming in us-east-1 (ADR-0010). Neural is the default engine: lower latency, USD 16 per million characters (generative USD 30) and no generative 'hallucinated speech' caveat. Voices and prices are packages/core/speech-voices.json, which the API reads too. dailyAlarmUsd mirrors the global daily AI cap in Admin > Settings: change both together.

distillation.note: Disabled on purpose: distillation runs from delayed per-conversation jobs the API enqueues, at session end and from the daily maintenance backstop (ADR-0018). A sweep that queries Aurora every 15 minutes keeps the cluster from pausing.

recordings.note: Call recordings (ADR-0023): the private recordings bucket accepts presigned uploads and replays only from these exact app origins (the CloudFront distribution's own origin; a custom site domain is added automatically). Recordings are kept for a year (packages/contracts RECORDING_LIMITS.retentionDays, not a setting), then the daily maintenance deletes them; the bucket's lifecycle expires anything left a week later.

media.note: The vEIR's face and voice. Face: HeyGen's stock avatar Thomas (Friendly), labelled AI avatar, in LITE, lip-syncing the ElevenLabs AI voice: the caller's page holds the avatar's speak channel (liteRoute browser; its origin wss://webrtc-signaling.heygen.io is in csp.connect) and forwards only units the server admitted; billed to the HeyGen account (LITE, 1 credit a minute; on the Free plan short sessions with the vendor's watermark, and when credits run out new sessions are refused and the call goes on with the presence and its own speakers), platform admins and people given face access only (docs/runbooks/avatars.md section 9). A real person's likeness is never fed by the browser. Voice: every call speaks with the ElevenLabs stock voice voiceId (Caleb, an ElevenLabs-made male library voice to match the male stock avatar, labelled AI voice; docs/runbooks/elevenlabs-voice.md says why this one and how to change it), model eleven_flash_v2_5, and Amazon Polly says any unit ElevenLabs fails on in fallbackVoiceId, a male Polly voice so a failure never switches gender (fallback polly; speech.enabled must stay true). The key is the GitHub secret ELEVENLABS_API, copied to foundry-ascent/media/elevenlabs by the Ops - sync ElevenLabs key workflow after the first deploy of this setting (until then every unit is Polly). provider elevenlabs-stock also voices an EIR's consented clone once cloned voices are on in Admin > Settings; provider polly turns ElevenLabs off. To give an EIR their own face (LITE, server relay): face.mode lite, no face.liteRoute, face.audience everyone, no face.stock, then switch faces on in Admin > Settings and mark the EIR's face ready in the studio. For the stock face in the vendor's own voice: face.mode full and no liteRoute. The API role can read only the secrets of the vendors set here.
